description:
Lough Eske Castle stands on the shore of its lake near Donegal Town, in County Donegal. The present castle was built in 1859–61 for Thomas Brooke to designs by the architect Fitzgibbon Louch, in a Tudor Revival or Elizabethan style with turrets, curvilinear gables and crenellated parapets. It is built of local sandstone, reportedly from a quarry near Frosses, and it replaced earlier houses on the same site, built in 1621 and 1751. The 1621 house was probably built for the Knox family, and the estate passed to the Brooke family by marriage in 1717.

In 1894 the estate was bought by Major General Henry George White; a Celtic-cross grave marker for him stands east of the house, and a ballroom wing was added in 1914. The Knee family ran the castle as a hotel from 1930 to 1939. A fire in 1939 left it largely burnt out, and it stayed derelict until about 2007.

Around 2007 it was rebuilt and extended as a hotel, with the façade recreated from the original designs, and it reopened in December 2007. Today it is a 5-star hotel with a restaurant, a spa, lakeside gardens and fishing on Lough Eske.

The remains of an earlier castle, traditionally associated with the O'Donnells of Tyrconnell, stand in the grounds east of the house, separate from the hotel building. The O'Donnells led resistance to English rule in the late 16th and early 17th centuries, a story that ended with the Flight of the Earls in 1607.

faqs.question: When was Lough Eske Castle built?
faqs.answer: The present castle was built in 1859–61 for Thomas Brooke to designs by the architect Fitzgibbon Louch. It replaced earlier houses on the same site, built in 1621 and 1751.

faqs.question: What happened to Lough Eske Castle in 1939?
faqs.answer: A fire in 1939 left the castle largely burnt out, and it stayed derelict until about 2007, when it was rebuilt and extended as a hotel. It reopened in December 2007.

faqs.question: Is the hotel the same building as the O'Donnell castle?
faqs.answer: No. The remains of an earlier castle, traditionally associated with the O'Donnells of Tyrconnell, stand in the grounds east of the house. The hotel is the 19th-century castle, rebuilt in 2007.

faqs.question: How far is Lough Eske Castle from Donegal Town?
faqs.answer: About 5 km north-east of Donegal Town, 4.7 km in a straight line, and roughly 10 minutes by car.

faqs.question: Who were the O'Donnells and why are they connected to Lough Eske?
faqs.answer: The O'Donnells were a Gaelic ruling family in Donegal. Tradition associates the remains of the earlier castle in the grounds with them; the hotel itself is a 19th-century building.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Donegal Town, about 10 minutes' drive.

**Rooms & rates:** Rooms spread across the main castle building, an adjacent wing, and Courtyard Suites converted from the old stables. From about €168 per night.

**On-site:** Fine-dining restaurant, spa, lakeside gardens, fishing on Lough Eske.

**Good to know:** The remains of an earlier castle, traditionally associated with the O'Donnells of Tyrconnell, stand in the grounds east of the house; they are not part of the hotel building.

**Combine with:** Donegal Castle in town, or the Donegal Bay coastal drive.
